reviewer_type: isolated AI reviewer, not human expert review
scope: One blind pass over the 32 shuffled cases, using only the three supplied local input files plus read-only primary records/notices. No repository, candidate labels/rationales, experiments, evaluated-model API, paid service or additional agents were used.
definitions:
Choose one label for the supplied claim relative to the supplied evidence packet.
solid: Claims accurately report the evidence with appropriate scope and caveats. Weak, observational, preclinical or mixed evidence can be reported accurately.
overclaim: The conclusion exceeds the evidence. This is the residual category for inflated framing, unsupported positive or negative generalization, extrapolation to unstudied populations, and surrogate endpoints presented as clinical outcomes.
correlation_vs_causation: A causal claim is drawn from a non-causal, uncontrolled or confounded design; correlation is treated as causation without the needed counterfactual/comparison.
mechanism_vs_evidence: A described biological mechanism (an animal or preclinical pathway) is used to imply human clinical benefit not demonstrated by the evidence. This includes animal-to-human therapeutic and preclinical-pathway-to-therapeutic leaps. A biomarker/surrogate-to-clinical gap alone is excluded from this category.
Precedence: A specific label (correlation_vs_causation or mechanism_vs_evidence) takes precedence over generic overclaim only when its defining trigger is present and captures the core error. Do not stretch a specific definition; otherwise use overclaim. If the claim is appropriately bounded by the evidence, use solid.
source_review_limitations: Primary article abstracts, identifiers and disclosed correction notices were checked; full article bodies, raw data and all figures/supplements were not exhaustively audited.
Most independent source retrieval used Europe PMC's indexed primary-article abstracts by PMID. Direct PubMed, PMC and JAMA record/notice content was also used for the flagged cases.
The JAMA PDF and direct PMC correction rendering initially failed; primary-site indexed notice text supplied the correction checks. Exact TEAM-AD old/new display values remain uncertain.
A no-retraction result in a linked-notice list is not a universal guarantee of source validity.
Historical publication dates do not by themselves identify the retrieved corrected/final content.

summary.candidate_label_disagreements: Not assessable: no candidate labels, candidate rationales or experimental results were supplied or inspected.
material_findings: CRASH-2 original-report citation should be rebound from West Indian Medical Journal PMID 21702233 to original Lancet PMID 20554319. Label is unaffected.
RECOVERY, TEAM-AD and screen-time source version fields are publication dates, not exact identifiers for final/corrected bodies. Current decisive body content matches the packets.
TEAM-AD correction scope is verified but individual corrected table/figure values were not independently recovered; those values are unused. Screen-time corrected decisive coefficients are verified.

All 32 packets are sufficient for the requested label under the supplied definitions. This is a bounded AI judgment, not validation by human experts or an independent full-text scientific peer review.

source_audits.supplied_title: Effects of tranexamic acid on death, vascular occlusive events, and blood transfusion in trauma patients with significant haemorrhage (CRASH-2) A randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
source_audits.verification_method: Independent read-only Europe PMC core-record retrieval by supplied PMID; compared indexed primary-article abstract with packet. Additional primary record/notice checks are listed where needed.
source_audits.decisive_content_comparison_detail: The supplied republication abstract contains numeric formatting corruption. The packet matches the independently verified original Lancet abstract at PMID 20554319, including the within-eight-hours criterion and 14.5% versus 16.0% mortality.
source_audits.indexed_notice_result: No retraction notice was returned in the independently retrieved linked-notice list. This is not an exhaustive postpublication validity review.
source_audits.exact_correction_or_packet_issue: The supplied URL/PMID 21702233 is a West Indian Medical Journal record dated December 2010, carrying the Lancet DOI and a republication of the trial abstract. Its indexed body has formatting errors (for example placebo mortality appears as 160%). The original Lancet record is PMID 20554319, epub 2010-06-14, print 2010-07-03. Its eligibility and mortality figures support the packet. Replace the URL, source title punctuation and version with the original record if the packet is intended to cite the original randomized report. This is a source-binding repair, not evidence supporting treatment after eight hours.
source_audits.correction_uncertainty: No formal correction was required to resolve the decisive figures; the original abstract was independently checked. The supplied reprint should not serve as an exact original-version citation.

source_audits.supplied_title: Effect of vitamin E and memantine on functional decline in Alzheimer disease: the TEAM-AD VA cooperative randomized trial.
source_audits.verification_method: Independent read-only Europe PMC core-record retrieval by supplied PMID; compared indexed primary-article abstract with packet. Additional primary record/notice checks are listed where needed.
source_audits.indexed_notice_result: Indexed erratum exists; independently checked notice content/scope as described.
source_audits.exact_correction_or_packet_issue: The JAMA correction notice confirms one erroneous Table 2 value and erroneous Figure 4/eFigure values, corrected online. The current indexed abstract confirms the established-AD population and ADCS-ADL difference used in the packet. The source version 2014-01-01 predates the 2014-03-19 correction; identify the body as the corrected online abstract. The abstract reports 613 randomized but 561 analyzed after exclusion of 52 without follow-up; the packet does not falsely claim all 613 were analyzed, though this is a useful completeness caveat.
source_audits.correction_uncertainty: The primary notice available through the web index states affected locations but does not list each old/new value. Direct PDF access was blocked. Exact table/figure changes remain unaudited; this cannot turn a treatment-of-existing-AD study into prevention in healthy people.

source_audits.verification_method: Independent read-only Europe PMC core-record retrieval by supplied PMID; compared indexed primary-article abstract with packet. Additional primary record/notice checks are listed where needed.
source_audits.indexed_notice_result: Indexed erratum exists; independently checked notice content/scope as described.
source_audits.exact_correction_or_packet_issue: The disclosed correction is real. The packet uses the corrected 36-month beta -0.06 (CI -0.10 to -0.01) and 60-month beta -0.08 (CI -0.13 to -0.02). The notice also describes five other figure-CI digit changes and a model-clarification sentence, with conclusions unchanged. The source version 2019-03-01 predates the correction posted 2019-03-25; identify the packet as a corrected online abstract. No numerical packet repair is indicated.
source_audits.correction_uncertainty: The correction text was obtained from indexed primary PMC content after direct rendering was challenged. The five other figure intervals and archived uncorrected displays were not individually re-audited; they are unused in the packet.
